_doc: The standard switching plan (ACCOUNTS_PLAN_BUILD_STANDARD_SWITCHING), read by switching_plan.py and slot_allocator.py. Rules are data; each carries its provenance: [O] owner's words, [C] his question-card pick, [D] delegated (ours, under design/RimMandrake/delegation_policy.md), [A] agent proposal he has not ruled. Account names are the switcher's non-secret registry labels (~/.claude-accounts/accounts.tsv); reset times are NEVER written here: they are read from account_usage.py every pass.
_owner: [O] 2026-10-28 10:15 PDT: 'Use up both lukas.mandrake and mandrake.system of course down to ~2% for safety. Make sure not to overshoot and get stuck even if there is a surprise long-running subagent. then go idle until 1pm when you switch over to system.mandrake. Once steven.lewis resets, switch over to it and use it until 50%. Then use up system.mandrake to 2%, then lukas.mandrake to 2%. That's our first "standard switching plan."'
_order: [R] coordinator 2026-10-28 10:58 (relayed rule change, superseding the fixed order of the 10:15 words): 'burn the account whose reset comes soonest among those still above their floor (use it or lose it), not a fixed order ... if lukas is still above 2% at 13:00, stay on lukas (it expires at 16:00) ... The pause-at-floor-until-a-reset step only applies when no account has budget left ... Order those by expiry too: at 14:45, lukas's leftover (expires 16:00) is spent before Steven's half'. The engine burns the eligible account whose budget EXPIRES soonest: a plain account's at its next weekly reset; steven's at the end of his window (his reset + window_h_after_reset), since that is when his half is lost to us ([A]: by his weekly reset system would outrank him, against the 10:15 order). This list only breaks ties.

steven._leave_pct_left: [C] 2026-10-28 10:20 card, Steven: 'Leave at 52% left' (his 10:15 words: 'use it until 50%'; the 2 points are the overshoot margin).
steven._window_h_after_reset: [O] 2026-10-27 'Dispatcher can use Steve up to 50% after a fresh reset only'; the 48 h reading of 'fresh' is [A] (slot_rules.json lent_accounts.steven.prefer_start_of_week_h). Outside this window the engine never switches to steven and switches off him if live.

floors._doc: [O] relayed by the coordinator 2026-10-28 11:2x: 'If it's actually safe to switch (is that because it goes through tailscale or something?) even when we hit 0%, then let it hit 0%. I thought it would lock us out'. The switch is local (claude-account swaps the credential file; no model tokens, no Tailscale), so an account we switch away from burns to 0%. [D] delegated: ops threshold (card 10:20, Floor: '[No preference]'; restated by the coordinator 11:2x): the account we idle on until a reset keeps 2%, so the owner can still talk to a seat while we wait. blind_zero_pct [R] coordinator 11:2x: once an account's last MEASURED reading is at or under 1%, a blind reading (failed /usage, usage-limit error, ESTIMATE, stale) counts as 0% and triggers the switch: never sit waiting on a meter that cannot read an exhausted account.

_soft_margin_pct: [C] card 10:20, Overshoot: 'Soft line, then hard stop'. At line + 2%: the allocator gives every seat 0 new helpers and the notice tells running ones to publish and finish.
_switch_lead_min: [A] a switch that a reset will cause (system at its reset, steven at his) raises the same soft notice this many minutes before the reset, so work is published before the windows close.

fresh._doc: [A] (brief 2026-10-28): within near_pct of a line, the engine polls the meter itself rather than trust a reading older than max_age_min.

_pool_pacing: [C] card 10:20, Pacing: 'Pace the whole pool BECAUSE it spreads out the human review time cleanly to inform the process in a timely manner.' slot_allocator paces on what this plan will still spend (steven down to its leave line inside its window, the others to their floors) over the hours to each deadline.

gate._doc: Cutover 2026-10-28: account_failover.py owns the machine until its stage 3 (back to system after the 13:00 reset) writes this marker with phase done. The engine stays passive until then; once seen it is remembered in the engine's own state, so retiring account_failover later does not re-gate it.
